title: School chemistry foundations
description: Element symbols and formulas, the mole, balancing equations and simple stoichiometry at the level of one year of school chemistry. This is the entry evidence for CHE-101; advanced mathematics does not establish it.

title: The mole and molar mass
description: Avogadro's number, formula and molar mass, converting between mass, amount and number of particles; percent composition and empirical formulas.

title: Chemical formulas and nomenclature
description: Molecular, empirical and structural formulas; ionic and molecular compounds; systematic names; atomic symbols with mass number, atomic number and charge; isotopes and average atomic mass.

title: Balancing chemical equations
description: Atom and charge conservation in chemical equations; phase labels; molecular, total ionic and net ionic equations.

title: Reaction stoichiometry
description: Stoichiometric factors from a balanced equation; mass-to-mass and mass-to-amount calculations with unit tracking and a mass-balance check.

title: Limiting reactant and yield
description: Identifying the limiting reactant, theoretical and percent yield, excess reactant remaining; the assumptions behind a yield calculation.

title: Solution concentration and dilution
description: Molarity, moles from volume and concentration, the dilution relation and solution stoichiometry.

title: The nuclear atom and the failure of classical physics
description: Discovery of the electron and the nucleus, the Coulomb force between electron and nucleus, and why a classical orbiting electron cannot be stable.

title: Photons and the quantisation of light
description: Wave properties of light, E = hν, the photoelectric effect and work function, line spectra as evidence for discrete energy levels.

title: Hydrogen atom energy levels and orbitals
description: E_n = −R_H/n² for one-electron atoms, emission and absorption transitions, ionisation energy, orbitals and quantum numbers, wave–particle duality of matter.

title: Multi-electron atoms and electron configurations
description: Shielding and effective nuclear charge, orbital energy ordering, aufbau, Hund's rule and the Pauli principle, configurations of atoms and ions, photoelectron spectroscopy as evidence.

title: Periodic trends
description: Atomic and ionic radii, ionisation energy, electron affinity and electronegativity across periods and down groups, with the subshell irregularities and the measurements that establish them.

title: Ionic bonding and lattice energy
description: Cation and anion formation, electron configurations of ions, lattice energy and the Born–Haber cycle.

title: Covalent bonding and Lewis structures
description: Electron sharing and the octet rule, the Lewis procedure, formal charge, resonance and delocalisation, bond polarity and exceptions to the octet rule.

title: VSEPR and molecular geometry
description: Electron-pair geometry versus molecular shape, the AXE notation, lone-pair repulsion and angle compression, molecular polarity from shape and bond dipoles.

title: Molecular orbital theory
description: Bonding and antibonding orbitals from atomic orbital combinations, MO diagrams for first- and second-period diatomics, bond order and magnetism.

title: Valence bond theory and hybridisation
description: Orbital overlap, σ and π bonds, sp, sp², sp³ and higher hybridisation schemes assigned from electron-pair geometry.

title: Enthalpy and thermochemistry
description: Heat, first law, enthalpy as a state function, standard states, bond enthalpies, enthalpies of formation and Hess's law, with the phase of every species stated.

title: Entropy, Gibbs free energy and spontaneity
description: Entropy and microstates, the second and third laws, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, temperature dependence of spontaneity and free energies of formation.

title: The equilibrium constant
description: Dynamic equilibrium, the reaction quotient Q, Kc and Kp with their reference states, ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q, ΔG° = −RT ln K, ICE-table calculations.

title: Le Châtelier's principle
description: Response of an equilibrium to changes in concentration, pressure or volume and temperature, explained through Q versus K and the temperature dependence of K.

title: Acid–base equilibria
description: Brønsted–Lowry acids and bases, Kw, pH, Ka and Kb, weak acid and base calculations, buffers and titration curves.

title: Oxidation–reduction and electrochemistry
description: Oxidation numbers, balancing redox equations by half-reactions, galvanic cells, standard potentials, ΔG° = −nFE° and the Nernst equation.

title: Transition metals and crystal field theory
description: d-block oxidation states, coordination complexes, d-orbital splitting in crystal field theory, colour and magnetism of complexes.

title: Reaction rates and rate laws
description: Average and instantaneous rates, rate expressions with stoichiometric coefficients, rate laws and orders determined from initial-rate data, units of rate constants.

title: Integrated rate laws and half-lives
description: Zero-, first- and second-order integrated rate laws, linear plots for determining order, half-lives and their concentration dependence.

title: Reaction mechanisms
description: Elementary steps and molecularity, rate-determining step, pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations, testing a mechanism against an observed rate law.

title: Temperature dependence of rates
description: Collision theory, activation energy, the Arrhenius equation and its two-temperature form, reaction coordinate diagrams, catalysts.

title: The kinetic view of equilibrium
description: A reversible reaction as competing forward and reverse rates: conservation of total concentration, relaxation to equilibrium, K = k_f/k_r for elementary steps, and the observations that distinguish dynamic equilibrium from no reaction.
